label: azure document-intelligence · 04 Base64 and custom target
info:
**Analyze an inline Base64 document into msg.result**

The inject carries a small one-page PDF with synthetic text as Base64; the node decodes and sends it and writes the result to `msg.result`.

**Prerequisites:** the `@faigle/node-red-contrib-azure-apps` package, an Azure AI Document Intelligence resource.

**Setup:** before you start Node-RED, set:
- `NODE_RED_EXAMPLE_AZURE_DOCUMENT_ENDPOINT`: your Document Intelligence endpoint (e.g. `https://<resource>.cognitiveservices.azure.com/`)

The authentication node **EDIT ME: example Document Intelligence identity** uses **Microsoft Entra ID** (the node requests
Entra tokens only): the node uses whatever identity the Node-RED process can obtain (environment variables, managed identity,
Azure CLI login). Run it under a **dedicated test identity** with access to that resource only. This example contains no secret.

If a variable is unset, the node that needs it reports what is missing and makes no request.

**Activation:** this tab is disabled, and its configuration nodes are on the same tab. Enable the tab, deploy, then click **Set Base64 document**.

**Effects:** Sends the inline document to Azure for analysis. Configure everything first: a node checks its fields when the flow reaches it, so earlier steps of a click may already have run. Nothing is rolled back.

**Expected result:** after Azure finishes (the node polls every 2 seconds), the Debug sidebar shows the analysis result object.

**Cleanup:** the flow provisions no Azure resource. Each analysis runs as an operation in the service, which keeps its result and bills it under its own rules; this flow does not remove either. Remove the sample document from your share or URL if you placed it there for this example.

**Not verified:** a real Document Intelligence resource or model, and whether Azure accepts this particular document (the tests fake Azure and the identity and treat the document as opaque bytes); behaviour in the editor.
